intervals.label: Fly's Eye operating
intervals.note: Sokolsky & Thomson (arXiv:0706.1248) say "The detectors were operated from 1982 to 1992"; Bertou et al. (astro-ph/0001516) say data taking "started ... in 1982". The Fly's Eye group's own final paper says 1981, used here; the start-year disagreement is recorded in the log.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: Start is the end year of the original experiment; HiRes succeeded it on the same site.

name: Fly's Eye air-fluorescence detector
notes: The placement site is an approximate region marker (see site:dugway-flys-eye).

summary.plain: A pair of mirror-and-camera "eyes" that photographed the faint glow cosmic-ray air showers leave in the night sky.
summary.technical: Air-fluorescence detector: Fly's Eye I with 67 mirrors (1.5 m diameter, 880 PMT pixels, full-sky coverage) and Fly's Eye II with 36 mirrors, 3.3-3.4 km away, giving monocular and stereo reconstruction at 1017-1020 eV.

technology.quote: The Fly's Eye is a compound eye of 880 photomultiplier tube (PMT) pixels
technology.value: Two compound eyes of spherical mirrors with photomultiplier-tube cameras that image the fluorescence light of air showers: Fly's Eye I (67 mirrors) and Fly's Eye II (36 mirrors).
